input: Create a photographic map of my neighborhood

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The geographic boundaries of 'neighborhood' vary wildly — a few blocks, a zip code, a named district — and this determines how many photos are needed and how long the project takes.
Knowing who this is for (personal keepsake, community sharing, a school project, a business) changes the tone, depth, and presentation of the map entirely.
The photographic style — candid street shots, architectural details, nature, people, landmarks — determines what to shoot and what to leave out.
The platform or format used to assemble the map (Google My Maps, a printed poster, a photo book, a website, a collage app) shapes every downstream step.
Whether this needs to be done by a specific date or season affects scheduling and the number of shooting sessions required.
Budget determines whether professional printing, paid software, or hiring a designer is on the table, or if this must be done entirely free.

Knowing what 'done well' looks like — a certain number of locations covered, a specific level of visual polish, community approval — sets the quality bar and defines when the project is truly finished.

gold.taskTitle: Create a photographic map of my neighborhood
gold.taskDescription: Capture and assemble a photo-based map that visually documents the user's neighborhood.

questions.title: What geographic area counts as your neighborhood?
questions.description: Define the boundaries — e.g., a few blocks around your home, a named district, or a full zip code — to determine how many locations need to be photographed.

questions.title: Who is this map being made for?
questions.description: Identify the intended audience or purpose — personal memory, a community group, a school project, a local business — as this shapes tone and depth.

questions.title: What kind of subjects should the photos focus on?
questions.description: Clarify the photographic style and subject matter — landmarks, street scenes, architecture, nature, local businesses, residents — to guide what to shoot.

questions.title: What format should the finished map take?
questions.description: Determine the output format — an interactive digital map, a printed poster, a photo book, a website gallery, or a social media post — as this dictates which tools to use.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or specific season you need this done by?
questions.description: Establish any time constraints or seasonal preferences (e.g., capturing fall foliage or a neighborhood event) to plan shooting sessions accordingly.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: Understand spending limits to determine whether paid tools, professional printing, or design help are options, or if the project must be completed at no cost.

questions.title: How will you know when the map is finished and good enough?
questions.description: Define the success criteria — a minimum number of locations, a level of visual polish, approval from a group — so there is a clear finish line for the project.
